insights.content: DTC #1 is 2-1 in 35B (W4 was a bye). Karen Kiyono and Claudia Hernandez (both +0.22 delta) are the emerging D1 pair. Shi Oskooi's lone S2 appearance was a win — she's a viable S2 option when deployed. The roster has solid depth but lacks a dominant singles player like Seda Sargsyan (DTC #2, 3.92) or Arika Carrier (TPC, 3.96).

The 4-1 loss to Red Rock CC #2 in W3 exposed DTC #1's ceiling. Red Rock #2 (4-0) is the class of 35B with Mary Lind (4-0), Julie MacDonald, and Shanna Toft all unbeaten. DTC #1 will face them again — a different gameplan is needed.

Most overrated dynamics in 3.5: Joann Komanowski (LTF, 3.54, 0-2, -0.27), Debi Marimberga (LTF, 3.44, 0-2, -0.27), Lisa Gobel (Spanish Trail #2, 3.54, 0-2, -0.20), Kelly Nguyen (DTC #3 35B, 3.34, 0-3, -0.27).

Most underrated in 3.5: Yan Uyeno (Red Rock #1, 3.55→3.94, +0.39), Arika Carrier (TPC, 3.60→3.96, +0.36), Hannah Stevens (Summerlin, 3.28→3.59, +0.31), Jill Morrison (Spanish Trail #1, 3.12→3.43, +0.31), Punam Patel (Desert Palm, 3.30→3.60, +0.30).

In 35B, the biggest threats: Arika Carrier (TPC, 3-0 at D1, near-4.0 level), Mary Lind (Red Rock #2, 4-0 everywhere), Melanie Isbell (Dragonridge, 3-0 at S1/S2). For DTC #1's S1 matchups, Stacie Corelle (1-1) will face these players — she needs to be 50% or better to stay competitive.

35A is dominated by Summerlin Arbors (3-1) and DTC #2 (3-1). Red Rock CC #1 is 1-3 but has the division's biggest riser in Yan Uyeno (4-0, +0.39). Spanish Trail #2 at 1-3 is heavily reliant on cross-listed 3.0 players.

sections.title: 04/18 — next match preview: DTC #1 vs DTC #3

insights.content: DTC #1 (2-1) faces DTC #3 (0-4) at home. DTC #3 is the weakest team in 35B — their roster is built from cross-listed 3.0 players who are overmatched. This should be a comfortable win.

DTC #3's D1 options: Anna Clark (1-2 in 3.5), Kelly Nguyen (0-3, -0.27 delta), LaCheyva Edmonis (0-3), or Alexandria Chang (0-1). All are losing. DTC #1's Karen Kiyono + Claudia Hernandez (both 2-1) should be heavily favored.

DTC #3's singles: Valerie Witherspoon (1-1 at S1/S2) or Tayoni Coleman (1-1). Stacie Corelle at S1 is a fair matchup against Witherspoon. If DTC #3 deploys Coleman at S1, that's a tougher line. S2 is winnable regardless.
Deploy Shi Oskooi at S2 if roster allows — her 3.0 form (4-0, +0.32) translates to 3.5 S2 competitiveness. She won her only 3.5 S2 match. This is an opportunity to build her 3.5 record.

DTC #1 should win 4-1 or 5-0. DTC #3's 0-4 record and negative deltas across the roster make every line favorable. The only risk is if DTC #3 deploys its strongest cross-listed players (Tayoni Coleman, Anna Clark) at the right lines.
vs DTC #3 (0-4). Heavily favored. Target 5-0 to build game differential for standings tiebreakers.

vs DRAGONRIDGE CC (3-1). A real test. Melanie Isbell (3-0 at S1/S2) is a singles threat. Maria Allen (2-0 at S1, cross-listed) could also play. D1 with Lorraine Yarde (2-0) is solid. Expect a 3-2 either way.
vs SPANISH TRAIL #1 (2-2). Sara Sager (3-1) is reliable but beatable. Chandra VanPaepeghem (3-0) is their danger player. DTC #1 should win 3-2 if they handle D1.
vs RED ROCK CC #2 (4-0). The toughest match on the schedule. RR#2 is the class of 35B. Mary Lind (4-0) and the deep roster make this a probable loss unless DTC #1 brings their best lineup.
vs SPANISH TRAIL #1 again. Second match against them. By this point lineup tendencies will be clear.

DTC #1 needs to go 3-2 or better in the remaining 5 matches to be in playoff contention. The key matches are Dragonridge (4/25) and Red Rock #2 (5/9). Win the DTC #3 and Spanish Trail matches (expected), split Dragonridge and one upset of Red Rock #2 to finish 2nd or 3rd.
